what: Screens (2026-10-19): the two reads FACTS-RUN left that a run call's later steps could also trust, measured or bounded before either was built. FACTS-PASS: the update's first pass reads w, m1 and m2 for their maxima and finiteness, which the call's own last commit wrote; firstpass.patch points those three reads at one untouched read-only zero page, the ceiling of the commit handing them on. WEIGHT-PANELS: every bf16 GEMM over a weight packs it into a B panel the update could have written when it wrote the weight; bounded from PACK-ATTR's in-step attribution, not built.
host: Intel(R) Xeon(R) Processor @ 2.10GHz container, 4 vCPUs, GCC 13.3, Python 3.11.15; head 9a702a4 with this commit's runtime/c in the working tree (df21dda56e866915, every record's host line); the libraries built as the comparison harness builds the trainer; indicative wall times, no PMU.
reading: FACTS-PASS's ceiling (firstpass-*.txt, the tree against the patched tree, the 9.84M decoder's step at 8 x 128 tokens under bf16+exp+reduce+attn, a step each in turn, the losses equal every round): x1.024 (95% interval 0.996-1.041, 46 of 80 rounds) at four threads, x1.037 (1.010-1.063, 19 of 24) at one. The A/A, two builds of this tree's runtime/c (aa-*.txt): x0.994 (0.978-1.009) and x1.009 (0.979-1.034). The ceiling is the first pass's three state streams -- §27 of BCIR_NDT_MEASURE_2026-10-12 put the first pass at its four streams' bound, 3.15 ms of the four-thread step -- and a build would add the maxima of what the commit stores to the commit's three instances, the inputs of adamw_bounded's overflow proof. At four threads the ceiling is not resolved; at one it is resolved against 1 but not apart from the A/A's band. Not kept; it reopens when the first pass's state streams are a share of the step this host resolves, a step a few times shorter or a host whose A/A pair resolves 1%.

WEIGHT-PANELS, not built: PACK-ATTR timed the packs inside the four-thread step (../../2026-10-18/panels/packs/attribution-t4.json): 8.15 ms of wall a step, the weights' B packs (the forward's and the input adjoints') 42% of their thread time, about 3.4 ms -- 4.3% of the 79 ms step, the most the update writing the weights' panels could remove before it pays for writing them: two layouts a weight (W as B for its input adjoint, and W^T as B for the forward, a layout no writer has), 39 MB more written a step and 39 MB more state. Its ceiling is the packs' 3.4 ms less those writes, for a new panel layout and the state to hold it. Not kept.

files.run.sh: the records in order (bash run.sh TMP from the repository root): the patch applied to a copy of runtime/c, then firstpass and the A/A at four threads and one
files.firstpass.patch: the ceiling experiment: the first pass's w, m1 and m2 pointed at one zero page (a read-only anonymous mapping), so the pass reads only the gradient from memory; every step of the bench still skips the preflight by adamw_bounded's proof, so the patched trainer computes the tree's state
files.pair.py: two trainer libraries' steps alternated in one process, the order reversed every round, their losses held equal every round: each arm's median step, A over B's median ratio, a 95% percentile-bootstrap interval and the rounds B won
files.firstpass-t4.txt, firstpass-t1.txt: the tree (A) against the patched tree (B), four threads 80 rounds, one thread 24
files.aa-t4.txt, aa-t1.txt: pair.py over two builds of this tree's runtime/c: the A/A the screen's ratio is read against
